To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the chemoattractor FMLP induces production of PIP 3 in human neutrophil granulocytes via the FMLP receptor (G-protein of the Gi type) and phosphatidylinositide 3 kinase gamma, and that the co-operation of this kinase with phosphatidylinosite transfer protein is necessary for FMLP-dependent production.

phosphoinositide (PI) 3-kinases (PI3Ks) and their lipid products phosphoinositides (PIs) are important regulators of neutrophil responses, and that PI transfer protein (Pitp) is involved in the regulation of PI3K activity.

phosphatidylinositide 3,4-5-triphosphate (PIP3), which plays an essential role in neutrophil activation by chemoattractants, is formed in the plasma membrane, and this process involves the chemoattractive receptor, heterotrmeric G-proteins, phosphoinositide-3-kinase-gamma (PI3Kgamma), and a phospholipid transfer protein, phosphatidylinostol transfer protein (PPT).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of PITP in the regulation of PIP3 formation.
the co-operation of PI3Kgamma with PITP in the production of PIP 3.
a new aspect of the regulation of PIP3 metabolism by the chemo-attractant receptor and its downstream signalling molecules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the FMLP-sensitive P3 production in neutrophils is a process involving the FMLP receptor and heterotrimeric Gi-protein.
FMLP-induced PIP3 production is a result of the co-operation between PITP, PI3K, and Gi proteins.
PITP is involved in the production of PIP(3) by PI3Kgamma in human neutrophil membranes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PITP is an essential factor for the production of PIP(3) by PI3Kgamma.
FMLP-sensitive production of PIP(3) in human neutrophil requires the presence of PITP in the plasma membrane.

FMLP-dependent production and degradation of PIP3 in human neutrophil membranes is regulated by the co-operative actions of PI3Kgamma/PITP, phospholipase Cbeta, GTPase-activating proteins, and phosphatases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PITP can act in concert with PI3Kgamma in the synthesis of PIP(3) in human neutrophil plasma membrane.
the co-operating action of PI3Kgamma with PITP is essential for the FMLP-sensitive production of PIP(3) in human neutrophil plasma membranes.
PITP is required for optimal production of PIP(3) by PI3Kgamma in permeabilized neutropils, suggesting a novel role for PITP in regulating PI3K activity.
